::: {.hub-summary}

This project has been a way for me to get accustomed to bioinformatics, and it aims at a
quantitative analysis of protein-coding conservation in human, mouse and macaque. It now
focuses on the transporters of the blood–brain barrier, the genes that decide whether a drug
can cross it.

:::

## What's currently being built

The first pipeline tried to score every BBB gene at once. The project now narrows to the
**transporters**, the solute carrier (SLC) and ATP binding cassette (ABC) families, which
decide whether a drug crosses the barrier and which [Song 2020](papers/song2020.qmd) and
[Miao 2026](papers/miao2026.qmd) both find diverging between mouse and human.

**The question.** For BBB transporters, does a difference in **expression** between species go
together with a difference in **coding sequence**, across human, macaque and mouse?

**The plan.**

1. **Replicate Miao et al. 2026** as a calibration: capillary endothelial expression in mouse
   and human, with one-to-one orthologues, Seurat, Wilcoxon and Bonferroni.
2. **Re-run sequence conservation on the transporter set**, reusing the clean steps of the
   [first pipeline](https://github.com/Mmynemious/BBB-Gene-Conservation/blob/main/archive/first_pipeline/AUDIT.md) and applying the audit fixes.
3. **Link expression and coding-sequence differences** gene by gene.
4. **Write the introduction**: why the barrier matters, and what species differences in it
   mean for drug delivery between human, mouse and macaque. **In progress.**

**Progress.** [Step 1, the transporter target list](method-driven-pipeline.qmd), is written up.

## Future work

Kept out of the current scope on purpose:

- **Phylogenetic dN/dS** with PAML across all three species, instead of pairwise estimates.
- **Regulatory and non-coding sequence**, where most differences in expression level are
  thought to live.
- **A macaque expression atlas**, so macaque expression is measured rather than inferred
  from mouse.
- **Endothelial subtypes** from the Wälchli atlas, to ask whether a transporter is
  capillary-specific rather than merely detected.

## The first pipeline

My first attempt scored every BBB gene at once. An audit of all 15 steps found three errors
that change its conclusions, and it is the reason the project now looks the way it does. The
pipeline, its results and the full audit are archived in the repository:
[first pipeline and audit](https://github.com/Mmynemious/BBB-Gene-Conservation/blob/main/archive/first_pipeline/README.md).
